clue.text: Liable, that's flat

blocks.note: first meaning: inclined or apt to do something
second meaning: lying face down, stretched out

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a verdict that something is liable and flat; the two words are separate meanings of one adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both a tendency towards something, as in prone to error, and lying face downward on the ground.

clue.text: For brevity, order 'spit and shine'

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them afresh, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sergeant, keeping it short, barks a command for spit and polish on boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit and shine' sounds like a parade-ground instruction; the order is really to rearrange the letters of spit and shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithiness is the quality of saying much in few words, which is concision or terseness of expression.

clue.text: Out of print time in the works

blocks.note: OP is the abbreviation for out of print
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A book that has gone out of print while still being prepared at the printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the works' looks like a phrase meaning in preparation, but 'the works' is the definition: opera is the Latin plural of opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus means a work, and its Latin plural is opera, so the word can stand for a set of compositions.

clue.text: Head, in the finish, gets comfortably settled

indicators.note: one word placed in another means the head word sits inside the word for finish

blocks.note: the end is the finish
sconce is an old jocular word for the head

explanation.surface: Someone's head, at the end of a long day, sinks comfortably into the pillow.
explanation.walkthrough: Sconce for head is an old humorous usage the solver may not know; the head word sits wholly inside the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ensconced is to be established snugly in a place, so it means safely and cosily installed.

clue.text: Raids on a hot spot by surprise

blocks.note: to bomb a place is to raid it from the air
hell is the proverbial hottest place

explanation.surface: Air raids are launched without warning on a dangerous trouble spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Raids is read as a verb, bombs, and the hot spot is hell, placed after it in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is an unexpected, shocking piece of news, so it is a figurative word for a startling event.

clue.text: Girl with pulling power finds yeast a help

blocks.note: barm is the froth on fermenting malt liquor, used as yeast
an aid is a help

explanation.surface: An attractive woman discovers that yeast helps her, perhaps in a beauty routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling power' suggests sex appeal, but the pulling is of beer pumps behind a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who serves drinks in a pub pulls pints on the beer pumps, which is the cryptic sense of pulling power.

clue.text: She used to petrify people by bearing jellyfish

blocks.note: the Gorgon of Greek myth whose gaze turned onlookers to stone
E for east is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A mythic woman turned people to stone simply by the way she carried herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like her deportment, but it is a compass point; jellyfish is plural, matching the Latin-style plural ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusae is the plural of medusa, the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a cnidarian, named after the snake-haired Gorgon.

clue.text: Islam changed the Indian summer capital

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A religion is said to have transformed a capital city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian summer' tempts as the phrase for a late warm spell; here it is a capital used by India's government in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Simla, now Shimla, in the Himalayan foothills, was where the British Raj moved its government during the hot months.

clue.text: Making an offer out of being helpful . . .

blocks.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex officio
tending is looking after, caring for

explanation.surface: Someone offers something purely from a wish to help, the dots leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue to the next in the surface only; each is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an invitation or hand is to hold it out, so extending means proffering something to another person.

clue.text: . . . after being dead right!

blocks.note: the late someone is someone who has died
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: an offer of help only comes once someone has died, and how true that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead right' reads as an exclamation of agreement; it splits into dead and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and after are both adverbs of time meaning at a subsequent point, so one can replace the other.

clue.text: It's certainly in step, dear

indicators.note: one thing being in another means the first words are set inside the word for a step

blocks.note: a tread is the flat part of a stair, a step
sure, as an answer, means it certainly is

explanation.surface: An affectionate assurance to a dancing partner that they are keeping in step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like an endearment addressed to someone; it is the definition, in its sense of precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dear to you is held precious and cherished, which is what treasured means as an adjective.

clue.text: Satisfied about Holy Writ in the anthem

indicators.note: about means around, so the satisfied word wraps round the scripture abbreviation

blocks.note: a demand that is satisfied has been met
OT is the Old Testament, part of Holy Writ

explanation.surface: A churchgoer content that the anthem's words come from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: MET goes round OT, the Old Testament abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition set to sacred words, much like a church anthem.

clue.text: State of a girl with a surprised expression

blocks.note: Ida is a girl's name
ho is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A description of how a young woman looks when taken aback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like her condition, but it is an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the north-western Rocky Mountain region.

clue.text: A born composer, one who restrains himself

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for born
Sir John Stainer, Victorian English composer of church music

explanation.surface: A musician by birth who keeps a tight rein on his own temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: Stainer wrote The Crucifixion, a staple of English church choirs.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refrains from something, especially alcohol, so he holds back his own appetites.

clue.text: Awful vice den revealed

indicators.note: something awful is a terrible mess, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful den of iniquity has been exposed, like a newspaper scoop.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or make evident a quality or feeling, so evinced means displayed or made plain.

clue.text: One sister, a little old-fashioned, gets overwhelmed

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a nun is a religious sister
slightly out of fashion is dated

explanation.surface: A nun with rather old ways finds herself swamped.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundated literally means flooded, and figuratively swamped with more than one can handle.

clue.text: Grudging two points to the competition

blocks.note: E and N, east and north, are two compass points
vying is contending or competing

explanation.surface: A sportsman resentfully conceding two points to a rival in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grudging' reads as conceding reluctantly; here it is the verb to grudge, to resent another's good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: To grudge someone something is to resent their having it, which is the sense of envying them.

clue.text: Having a coat on, dis appeared round the river

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the vanishing word wraps the river

blocks.note: split into one word, disappeared means vanished
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone in a coat appeared, then disappeared, around a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The split 'dis appeared' is to be read as one word, disappeared, which is the trick of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnished wood has a protective coat of varnish over it, so a coat here is a layer of finish.

clue.text: Fuel cover in old lighter

blocks.note: gas is a fuel
a mantle is a cloak, a covering

explanation.surface: Fuel is covered up inside an old cigarette lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' suggests a cigarette lighter; it is something that gives light.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas mantle is the glowing mesh hood fitted over a gas jet in old gas lamps to give bright light.

clue.text: Herd of swine, with a duck in separate surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings enclose something, so the word for separate wraps round the duck

blocks.note: to sunder is to separate
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Pigs and a duck kept apart in different pens on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batsman's score of zero, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounder is the old collective noun for a group of wild boar or pigs, as a pride is for lions.

clue.text: Excellent specimen of a snake

blocks.note: first meaning: informal for a first-rate example of something
second meaning: a rattlesnake

explanation.surface: A naturalist admires a particularly fine snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for something splendid, and an American short name for the rattlesnake.

clue.text: Puts under cover the fish, taking a long time

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
ages is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone slowly hiding away a catch of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To garage a car is to put it in a shelter, so garages means stores under a roof.

clue.text: How my sainted Aunt behaves?

blocks.note: surface reading: 'my sainted aunt' is an exclamation of surprise, so this seems a puzzled question
setter's reading: an aunt who is a saint would conduct herself in a pious way

explanation.walkthrough: 'My sainted aunt!' is a mild old exclamation; taken literally, a saintly aunt behaves in a devout manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes acting in a pious, devout way, as a holy person would conduct herself.

clue.text: With police back in, calmed down and retired

indicators.note: going back means the police letters are read from right to left
in means the police abbreviation is placed inside the word for calmed down

blocks.note: a storm that has abated has calmed down
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detective police

explanation.surface: With police back on the scene, things settled down and everyone went home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests going to bed or giving up work; here it is a monarch stepping down.
explanation.definitionFit: A king who abdicated gave up the throne, which is a formal resignation or withdrawal from office.

clue.text: Girl making a foolish start

blocks.note: first meaning: a girl's name
second meaning: the month that begins with a day for playing pranks

explanation.surface: A young woman makes a silly beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The month opens on the first, the day for practical jokes, and it is also a girl's given name.

clue.text: A game for men!

blocks.note: surface reading: a sport meant for males only
setter's reading: the pieces of this board game are called men

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests a manly pastime; in fact the pieces on a board are commonly called men.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game of kings, queens and pawns uses pieces traditionally called men, so it is played with them.

clue.text: The answer is below (5

blocks.note: surface reading: the solution appears further down the page
setter's reading: the answer is the Latin word for below

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a pointer to a solution printed further down; instead the answer is a Latin word meaning below, as in see infra.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra is Latin for underneath, used in footnotes and as a prefix meaning beneath, as in infrared.

clue.text: Start with nothing in the kitty

indicators.note: in means the nothing is placed inside the word for kitty

blocks.note: a kitty is a pool of money, a fund
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone starts a game with an empty kitty.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside FUND, after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a company or school is to establish it, so it means to set up or begin something.

clue.text: Despicable fellow — he's coming early

blocks.note: a rat is a contemptible person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nasty character is turning up ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Rathe is an archaic or poetic word, as in Milton's 'rathe primrose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an old poetic adjective for things that appear or bloom early in the season.

clue.text: Jenny kissed him!

blocks.note: surface reading: gossip that a girl called Jenny kissed some man
setter's reading: Jenny kissed me is the first line of a famous short poem, whose writer is the man kissed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny kissed me when we met' is the well-known 1838 rondeau said to be about Jane Carlyle kissing its poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Romantic essayist and poet wrote Jenny Kiss'd Me, so he is the man the clue says was kissed.

clue.text: Badly misguided, in later days, anyway

indicators.note: any way means in any order at all, so the letters may be rearranged freely

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who, in old age at least, has gone badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition; the signal is 'anyway', read as any way.
explanation.definitionFit: To be led astray is to be drawn into error or bad ways by someone else's influence.

clue.text: Trick shuffle

blocks.note: first meaning: a crafty ruse or ploy
second meaning: evasion, shifting about to avoid something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trick shuffle' sounds like a card sharp's move; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a clever ruse, and as a verb to evade or shift aside, as shuffle can mean to prevaricate.
